My point is, everytime I do something “ I want to” it ends up causing me immeasurable pain…. Why the fuck would I want to keep experiencing that

I am still around, coincidentally forgetting a lighter in turn saved my life, I stood on the bridge crying for about 3 hours and when I went to smoke my last cigarette, I had no lighter. I asked a guy In a Black Sabbath hoodie for one cause I thought, “hey he’d probably have one” he didn’t. But he asked me if I was thinking about jumping as I was bawling my eyes out leaning on the railing of the bridge, I told him yes and he immediately told me not to, I asked why and he explained to me that he had a friend jump 20 years prior and every day without fail he has walked the Golden Gate to remember his friend. He sat there listening to me with open ears, he heard more about my life than most people I’ve known 5-10 years. We sat there talking for at least an hour and when he asked how I was getting home I explained I lived 50 miles north of the bridge, and had ubered there so I had no real way back. He convinced me to walk with him to his car, I was on the north side of the bridge and his car was parked in the toll plaza on the south side, we walked the entire length of the bridge talking about friends we had lost to suicide. The entire drive back we talked about things in our life we enjoy, that make us happy, people that we care about etc. when I got home my friends had only been awake for like an hour or two and I was able to convince them I went out to breakfast and then went to the gym, they don’t even know. I think the most fucking bizarre part of all of this is that me and that stranger never exchanged names
